  createDatabase(
    name: $name
    databaseName: $databaseName
    databaseUser: $databaseUser
    ownerId: $ownerId
    environmentId: $environmentId
    plan: $plan
    version: $version
    diskSizeGB: $diskSizeGB
    public: $public
  ) {
    id
    name
    databaseName
    databaseUser
    plan
    status
    projectId
    environmentId
    __typename
  }
}

scopeNotes: Exact matching native GraphQL operation requests and complete responses are retained, without auth headers, cookies, credentials or connection URIs. SQL uses the ordinary CNPG application connection; no role or privilege changes were requested.
Kubernetes conditions/error log/cleanup attached below are explicitly selected projections, not complete Kubernetes responses.

No response interception, artificial server latency, SQL sleep, concurrent human writer or automatic retry was added. The queued code only observes natural Available then clicks the normal SQL controls.
The desktop first30s observation chunk remained Creating. Its second chunk waited17.436s for Available. Mobile started alreadyAvailable:false on a fresh390px document.

42501 and23505 are distinct observed SQLSTATEs; the mobile filtered PostgreSQL record specifically identifies pg_extension_name_index/extname vector. No further catalog internals or privilege mechanism is inferred.

Settled retries are labeled controls: both catalogs later report true, both identical migrations succeed and both vector-distance results equal1. This is not a never-installed extension or a missing package.

Only fresh default-identity Free/private PostgreSQL18 was exercised. Other majors/plans, custom identities, restore/import, initial suspend/resume, hosted pre-fix backfill, external CLI and live MCP/REST status parity remain unverified here.

w8/m84 owns installation and hosted existing-parent backfill. Its installer/ExtensionsReady verdict are working. This residual is first Core Ready/Available publication, which does not consume that verdict; no pending first-availability task was found in the indexed91 open/blocked milestones.
The a867 readiness timestamp lead alone was not a reproduction. The two a868 native failures are the evidence.
The mobile screenshot was opened and inspected, but remains a local ignored supplement. Durable mobile ARIA and native/API/log evidence support the finding without the PNG.
Console/network were captured after cleanup/logout. Native GraphQL HTTP200 errors are preserved separately; aborted navigation records are not classified as an independent bug.

No product fix was implemented. No paid or foreign resources were changed. Both exact database IDs and all7 baseline ID sets are checked below; provider disk erasure beyond PVC removal is not claimed.

matches: Every Database reconcile applies an owned `postgresql.cnpg.io/v1` Database child `<db>-app` (`database_extensions.go`) adopting the application database (its recorded name and owner; restores copy the source's) with `extensions: [{name: vector, ensure: present}]`, `ensure: present`, `databaseReclaimPolicy: retain` and no pinned version. CNPG installs vector as superuser, so the owner's `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector` becomes a no-op. The verdict projects onto a new `ExtensionsReady` condition (Pending/Applied/ApplyFailed — failure read regardless of generation since CNPG bumps observedGeneration only on success; ApplyError on a write error; ReservedDatabaseName for a PostgreSQL-owned name, which gets no child). The child never fails the Database. Watched via `Owns` (resourceVersion), RBAC (`config/rbac/role.yaml`, day-to-day read role) and the operator object-namespace admission policy cover `databases`.
